findings.title: Installer/OAuth-user check is skipped when no Integration row exists
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, when Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist, the view calls pipeline.next_step() without comparing the OAuth-authenticated user to the installation sender. This is the fresh-install path and is reachable before/asynchronously to the GitHub installation webhook that records metadata['sender']; build_integration then creates the integration from the API. A user who supplies another installation_id can therefore finish the pipeline without the new check ever running, so the advertised security fix can be bypassed. This branch should fail closed or obtain a trusted installer identity when no Integration/sender is available.

findings.title: Sender metadata is assumed to exist and can cause a 500 on reinstall
findings.body: The comparison dereferences integration.metadata['sender']['login']. Not every Integration has this structure: build_integration only adds metadata['sender'] when pipeline state contains a sender, and integrations created through the pipeline fallback (as exercised by assert_setup_flow) or older integrations can lack it. On a reinstall where the Integration exists but its OrganizationIntegration is gone, this raises KeyError and returns a 500 instead of the intended invalid-request page. Use .get('sender', {}).get('login') and reject with ERR_INTEGRATION_INVALID_INSTALLATION_REQUEST when it is missing.

findings.title: User-mismatch test can pass via state validation, not the new security check
findings.body: test_github_user_mismatch switches to user_2, starts a new pipeline with init_path_2, then calls the callback with the hardcoded state from the first user's pipeline. Pipeline signatures are tied to the pipeline/session, so the request will normally fail OAuthLoginView's state check before GitHubInstallation reaches the sender comparison. Since the test only asserts the generic 'Invalid installation request.' message used for both failures, it can pass without exercising the new mismatch check. Capture/follow the redirect from init_path_2 to get the correct state, and assert that the failure came from the user comparison.

findings.title: Installation-not-found test no longer exercises the 404 path
findings.body: test_installation_not_found now sends state=ddd023... which is not the signature for the pipeline it just started, so OAuthLoginView rejects the request before build_integration calls /app/installations/{id}. The assertion was also changed from 'The GitHub installation could not be found.' to the generic invalid-request text. As a result, the 404 installation-not-found path is no longer covered; use the actual pipeline state and keep the specific assertion.
